resources.string: How these are calculated: BMI = weight (kg) / height (m) squared. BMR uses the Mifflin-St Jeor equation, which estimates the calories your body burns at rest. TDEE = BMR multiplied by your daily activity level (1.2 to 1.725). Your calorie target adjusts TDEE for your goal (for example, 20% lower for weight loss, never below 1200 kcal or your BMR). Protein, carbs and fat are set as a share of that target (4, 4 and 9 kcal per gram).
Exercise and calorie suggestions are estimates, not medical advice. Exercises were filtered using the limitations you entered. If you have an injury or medical condition, check with a professional.

Rest days are when your body adapts and gets stronger.

• Take a light walk or stretch for 10 minutes
• Drink water and eat enough protein
• Aim for 7 to 9 hours of sleep
• If you feel sore, do gentle mobility work instead of heavy training

These numbers are estimates from general formulas, not medical advice. BMI cannot tell muscle from fat. If you are under 18, pregnant, injured, have a medical condition, or have a history of disordered eating, talk to a doctor or registered dietitian before changing your diet or training.
